formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the spender's allowance over the owner's CSWUSDC vault shares (18 decimals) to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance. A value of 0 revokes it; type(uint256).max never decreases when spent.
Lets anyone submit the signature on chain up to `deadline`. The allowance it creates does not expire.
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce, which cancels any other pending permit signed with the same nonce.
Moves no tokens itself, but the spender can then move up to `value` of the owner's shares, for example to redeem them for USDC or put them in the withdrawal queue.
formats.shown: "Approve <amount> CSWUSDC for <spender> until <deadline>", with the share owner, spender, allowance amount (Unlimited at max), signature deadline and nonce all shown.

findings.title: Permit intent says the approval lasts 'until {deadline}', but only the signature expires; the allowance stays forever.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json interpolatedIntent "Approve {value} for {spender} until {deadline}". In ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit, the deadline is only checked against block.timestamp when the signature is submitted, then _approve(owner, spender, value) sets an allowance with no expiry. Case 3 shows "Approve Unlimited CSWUSDC for 0x494D… until 2030-01-01", which reads as an unlimited approval that ends in 2030.
findings.fix: Use "Approve {spender} to spend {value}; signature valid until {deadline}", or drop the deadline from the interpolated intent and keep it in the 'Signature deadline' field.
